context: Tests: removing static calls, singletons and direct time access (hidden dependencies) from business logic.

checklist.name: Inventory abstracted behind an interface
checklist.description: `OrderProcessor` calls an injected inventory interface instead of the static `InventoryChecker.isAvailable`

checklist.name: Payment injected
checklist.description: `new PaymentService()` no longer appears in `process`; a payment gateway interface is received through the constructor

checklist.name: Notification singleton removed
checklist.description: `NotificationService.getInstance()` is replaced by an injected notification port

checklist.name: Clock injected
checklist.description: `new Date()` is replaced by an injected `Clock` (or equivalent) so the timestamp is deterministic in tests

checklist.name: All dependencies in the constructor
checklist.description: The constructor lists every collaborator, with no hidden dependencies left in method bodies

checklist.name: No static or singleton access remains
checklist.description: The refactored file contains no static calls or `getInstance()` for behaviour

checklist.name: Behaviour preserved
checklist.description: The order is still only charged and confirmed when inventory is available, and `processedAt` is still set

checklist.name: Unit test uses simple doubles
checklist.description: The test passes a stub, fake or spy through the constructor and needs no static-mocking library

checklist.name: Fixed clock used in the test
checklist.description: The test supplies a fixed time and asserts the exact `processedAt` value

checklist.name: Does not weaken the design
checklist.description: The answer fixes the coupling rather than adding a test-only hook, flag or global override
